children: , the global payments and identity network, joined Ant International and Visa in building a common trust framework for the coming wave of AI-powered commerce. Shares slipped approximately 0.1% to $564.54.

The Know-Your-Agent approach is designed to make verified identity signals portable across card networks, digital wallets, agent platforms and online marketplaces. The idea is straightforward: establish who operates an AI agent, apply shared certification standards and continuously monitor transactions while leaving final approval decisions with each participant. That could strip away repetitive verification work and make it faster for merchants and AI platforms to launch agent-driven payment services.

The bigger question is whether interoperability turns into meaningful transaction growth for Mastercard rather than simply creating another industry standard. No pricing, payment-volume or revenue commitments were disclosed, so adoption will matter more than the announcement itself. The valuation picture adds another angle: at $564.54, Mastercard trades 17.46% below the GF Value estimate of $683.92, suggesting the market price remains well below GuruFocus' calculated fair-value benchmark despite the company's push deeper into agentic commerce.

title: Mastercard Slips as AI Agents Seek Shared Credentials
